I've been farming these 5 mu for 35 years, same wheat-maize rotation my father did. Let me think through this year.

For **winter wheat** — I planted it last October already, so I'm just managing now. I use Jimai 22, the improved variety the seed shop sells. Everyone around here uses it, gives good yield. Last year I got about 450 kg/mu, decent enough.

Fertilizer — I put down compound fertilizer (diammonium) before planting, about 40 kg/mu, then I topdress with urea at jointing stage, around 20 kg. So that works out to about 28 kg N, 8 kg P, 6 kg K per mu. My soil here is not bad, been farming it long time. I won't cut back because wheat is my food and my income — if I lose yield I lose more than the fertilizer cost.

Irrigation — I have the well, so I water 3 times: overwintering, jointing (green-up), and grain filling. If spring is dry, maybe 4 times. Pesticide I spray 2 times, once for aphids and once for wheat scab when flowering.

For **summer maize** after wheat harvest in June — I do no-till, just drill seeds into the wheat stubble with the machine service. Cheaper than ploughing and saves time. I plant Zhengdan 958 or similar hybrid, everyone uses hybrid now, traditional seeds nobody plants anymore.

Maize needs less fertilizer than wheat because summer rain helps. I side-dress urea once at big flare stage, about 30 kg. Plus a bit of compound at planting. Roughly 22 kg N, 6 kg P, 5 kg K per mu. Maize yield here is usually better than wheat, 550-600 kg/mu if weather cooperates.

Irrigation on maize — usually 1 time if July is dry, sometimes I don't need to water if rain is enough. Pesticide 2 times, for corn borer and armyworm.

5 mu is small. My wife and I work it, kids are in town with jobs. I don't waste money but I don't starve my crops either. Same as last year, same as neighbors.
